newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar locked in narrow range vs yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar locked in narrow range vs yen in Tokyo.

text.p: 0130 GMT --*Dollar stalled vs yen in mid-morning Tokyo amid dearth of incentives before U.S. June payroll data at 1230 GMT.
*Persistent exporter offers checked dollar's rise above 114.70 yen, while talk of bids by Japanese investors made dollar solid at around 114.30 yen, dealers said.
*Japanese exporters ready to sell dollars on rises if strong U.S. payroll data lifts dollar up.
*"Since exporters are trying to sell on rises after the job data, the topside will be limited at 115.20 yen in the near term," said a U.S. bank dealer.
*Since dollar failed to rise above 115.50 yen earlier this week, exporters decided to sell dollars near 115.00 yen, the U.S. bank dealer said.
*Many exporters have already arranged forward dollar sales covering period to end-August, but have not done so for period after September, he added.

*Japanese carmarkers keen to sell marks against yen on rises in crosses but have failed to do so amid recent weakening of mark against major currencies because of growing view that European single currency will start on time, said a European bank dealer.
*Dollar edged lower against mark in early Tokyo on Thursday due to profit-taking following overnight rallies, breaking through key resistance of 1.75 marks on options-related buying.
*Interbank dealers sold dollars slightly against yen on speculation that greenback's upside would be limited due to heavy selling orders by exporters and institutional investors.
*Speculative sales by U.S. operators also depressed dollar against yen in morning.
*But wait-and-see mood was strong ahead of U.S. payroll data due at 1230 GMT.
